title: /ops View as user: only owners and admins open a view of a customer, it never touches the admin's own sign-in or the customer's activity, dsh's socket opens as the customer, and it ends on exit or sign-out
steps: S1: POST /api/ops/view-as as a customer, a developer seat, and an owner from a foreign origin; as an owner with an over-long reason; and as an owner for a staff account, for themselves and for an unknown email.
S2: As an owner, open a view of a customer with no reason, then read /auth/me, open the customer's Inbox, and read /api/ops/ui with both cookies; open a socket with both cookies.
S3: Press the bar's exit, and separately sign out, with a view open; read the audit rows and read /auth/me with the old view token.
expect: S1: every attempt is refused (403, 400 or 404) and no audit row exists.

S2: the start answers a url, sets only tracy_view and writes a view_as.start audit row with the admin and the target; /auth/me answers the customer with viewAs.by the owner and renews nothing; the Inbox saves no language on the customer; /api/ops/ui still answers 200 for the admin; the socket is opened as the customer's email.
S3: exit answers 303 to /ops and sign-out clears tracy_view; each leaves a view_as.end audit row; the old view token reads as signed out.
fence: The view token (lib/session.js), the banner and scope (lib/view-as-guard.js), the start/exit doors (ops/view-as.js) and the socket identity (workspace/upgrade.js), driven through the real app on a scratch Postgres

tests: only an owner or admin, from this origin, may open a view
exit ends the view on the record
signing out ends an open view
/ops keeps the admin as the admin
a view token wins over the admin
a socket opened during an admin view
